title: que + mood = the fact that; si + past mood (if I could…); hubiera; the -ase / -iese form

cards.title: que + mood = 'the fact that'
cards.body: Starting a sentence with que + mood tense gives the feeling of 'the fact that you might have…'.

examples.en: That you bought it isn't my problem.
examples.es: Que lo compraras no es mi problema.

examples.en: That you told him isn't my problem.
examples.es: Que le contaras no es mi problema.

cards.title: Hypothetical si → past mood tense
cards.body: English does it too ('if I WERE you'). Poder's dot-past stem becomes pud-: pudieron → pudiera.

examples.en: If I could cook, I would.
If I could cancel it, I would.
If you'd told me, I would have gone.
examples.es: Si me lo hubieras contado, habría ido.

examples.en: If we'd known, we'd have gone.
If you saw it, you'd understand it. (formal)
examples.es: Si lo viera, lo comprendería / entendería.

cards.title: The alternative form: -ase / -iese
cards.body: Hablase = hablara, comiese = comiera, comiésemos = comiéramos. Same meaning; how much it's used depends on dialect. Recognise it, but you don't need to use it.
